Select 'Home To Z Pulse [1]' option to home the machine to the encoder's Z pulse. Also, the 'Encoder Is Used [1]' option must be selected with "Use Encoder" parameter.

If the quadrature encoder is used, select 'Enocoder Is Used [1]' to enable encoder inputs. Also, enter a valid value for the encoder resolution to "Encoder Resolution" parameter. If the quadrature encoder is not used, select 'Encoder Not Used [0]' option.

Select 'Encoder Is Used [1]' to enable the built-in absolute or quadrature encoder. Also, select encoder resolution from "Encoder Resolution" parameter. If the built-in encoder is not used or not available, select 'Encoder Not Used [0]' option.

Select 'Backplane Proximity Not Used' if the Backplane Proximity bit is not used when homing the module. If the Backplane Proximity bit is used when homing the module, select 'Backplane Proximity Used [1]'. For more info see the User Manual.

Select 'Stall Detection Disabled [0]' to disable motor stall detection. Select 'Stall Detection Enabled [1]' to enable motor stall detection. This functionality is valid only if encoder is used with valid encoder resolution.
To disable unit's antiresonance feature select 'Antiresonance Disabled [1]' option. To enable unit's antiresonance select 'Antiresonance Enabled [0]' option.

It determines the active state of Input 1. Select 'Input Active Low [0]' if your sensor has Normally Closed (NC) contacts and the input is active when there is no current flow through it. Select 'Input Active High [1]' if your sensor has Normally Open (NO) contacts and the input is active when current flows through the input.

It determines the active state of Input 2. Select 'Input Active Low [0]' if your sensor has Normally Closed (NC) contacts and the input is active when there is no current flow through it. Select 'Input Active High [1]' if your sensor has Normally Open (NO) contacts and the input is active when current flows through the input.

It determines the active state of Input 3. Select 'Input Active Low [0]' if your sensor has Normally Closed (NC) contacts and the input is active when there is no current flow through it. Select 'Input Active High [1]' if your sensor has Normally Open (NO) contacts and the input is active when current flows through the input.

It determines the active state of Input 3. Select 'Input Active Low [0]' if your sensor has Normally Closed (NC) contacts and the input is active when there is no current flow through it. Select 'Input Active High / STO [1]' if your sensor has Normally Open (NO) contacts and the input is active when current flows through the input, or if you are configuring the SV160x2-STO unit.

It determines the active state of Input 4. Select 'Input Active Low [0]' if your sensor has Normally Closed (NC) contacts and the input is active when there is no current flow through it. Select 'Input Active High [1]' if your sensor has Normally Open (NO) contacts and the input is active when current flows through the input.

It determines the active state of Input 4. Select 'Input Active Low [0]' if your sensor has Normally Closed (NC) contacts and the input is active when there is no current flow through it. Select 'Input Active High / STO [1]' if your sensor has Normally Open (NO) contacts and the input is active when current flows through the input, or if you are configuring the SV160x2-STO unit.

Only used when "Binary Iput Format" and/or "Binary Output Format" parameters are set to [1]. Select 'Little Endian [0]' to have 32-bit values transmitted in little endian format. Select 'Big Endian [1]' to have the 32-bit values transmitted in big endian format.
Select 'Little Endian [0]' to have 32-bit values transmitted in little endian format. Select 'Big Endian [1]' to have the 32-bit values transmitted in big endian format.

Select 'Multi-Word Format [0]' to program the Target Position and Programmed Speed parameters in Multi-Word Format. Select 'Signed 32-bit Integer Format [1]' to program the Target Position and Programmed Speed parameters in signed 32-bit integer format with the location of LSB determined by the "Binary Endian" parameter.

Select 'Multi-Word Format [0]' to have the Motor Position, Encoder Position, and Trapped Encoder Position reported in the Multi-Word Format. Select 'Signed 32-bit Integer Format [1]' to have the Motor Position, Encoder Position, and Trapped Encoder Position reported in signed 32-bit integer format with the location of LSB determined by the "Binary Endian" parameter.

When "Output 1 Action at Connection Lost" parameter is selected to be 'Set Output 1 to the State defined at Connection Lost [1]', Output 1 will be set to the state of this parameter: 'Low Output [0]' or 'High Output [1]'.
Either select 'Keep Output 1 at its last value [0]' or select 'Set Output 1 to the State defined at Connection Lost [1]' that is specified in the "Output 1 State at Connection Lost" parameter.

Select 'Fault Output [0]' to configure Output 1 to be a Fault Output. Select 'General Purpose Output [1]' to configure Output 1 to be a general purpose output whose state is determined by a bit in the Command Mode Network Output Data.
Commanded motion jumps from rest to the Starting Speed and then accelerates to the programmed speed. This value must be lower than velocity value of all performed moves.
Defines the number of steps needed to move motor's shaft by one turn.
Enter the value for the "Encoder Resolution" for the encoder that is attached to the motor. Must be set to four times the encoder's resolution.
Must be 2048 for built in absolute encoders, or 1024, 2048, or 4096 for built in incremental encoders.

Enter the value for the "Idle Current Percentage", from the given value range, that is suitable for your application. The value determines percentage of the "Motor Current X 10" parameter value when the motor is idling.
Enter the value for the "Motor Current X 10" parameter, from the given value range, that is suitable for your application.

Matches the driver to the motor. The motor may stall during high speed and/or high acceleration moves if the value is too low. The motor will make a high pitch noise while idling if the value is too high.
Enter the value for the "Hybrid Control Gain" parameter, from the given value range, that is suitable for your application.
Counts Per Revolution is a fixed number (16384) that cannot be changed.

This parameter defines the rate at which the servo will decelerate during all immediate stop conditions. These include, the Immediate Stop Command, Estop input, or if a CW or CCW Limit is reached. If you enter 0 value, the servo will use its default value for this parameter, which is 8,000 steps/ms/sec. Or, you can enter any other value from the given range of 1,500 - 15,999 steps/ms/sec.
Value of this parametar will limit continuous torque of steady running servo motor. It must be lower or equal to the value of Peak Torque Limit parametar.
Value of this parametar will limit peak torque of accelerating or decelerating servo motor. It must be higher or equal to the value of Continuous Torque Limit parametar.
Zero (0) value disables functionality of this parametar. To enable its functionality, enter any value from allowed range of 550 - 1000 that corresponds to voltage range of 55 - 100V.

Higher values of this parameter will cause the motor react faster but could lead to oscillations and instability. Lower values will make the motor react slower and will lead to higher velocity errors.
Increasing this parameter will bring velocity error down to zero but could lead to oscillations and instability.

This parameter sets the time constant for Low-Pass filter in the Velocity Feedback. A value of 0 means no filtering. Higher values will provide more filtering, but will also introduce delays that could lead to oscillations and instability.
Higher values of this parameter will make the motor react faster but could lead to overshoots. Lower values will make the motor to react slower and will lead to higher position errors.
This parameter is needed to force the steady state position error to zero.
This parameter is needed for a dumping action as the response could become oscillatory.
This parameter limits the position difference between actual and command values. A stall detection error will occure if the position difference exceeds this limit.

This parameter is used only with the STO version of the servo motor. It determines a Discrepancy or Mismatch time of STO inputs. Zero (default) value means that the Discrepancy time WILL NOT be monitored. Allowable values are from 50ms to 3000ms.
This is the Position Loop Proportional Gain applied when the servo is at rest. A default value of zero means that an internally calculated value is applied.
This is the Position Loop Integral Gain applied when the servo is at rest. A default value of zero means that an internally calculated value is applied.
